title: Grand Fir: Tall Grand Firs You Can Visit
meta_description: A Pacific Northwest fir that grows fast and tall. At Ardkinglas in Argyll, one planted around 1875 was measured at 64.8 metres in 2025.
intro: The grand fir comes from the Pacific Northwest, from Oregon to British Columbia, and it grows tall fast enough that European foresters have planted it since the nineteenth century for exactly that. Scotland holds the giants. At Ardkinglas in Argyll, a sapling that went into the Pinetum around 1875 was measured at 64.8 metres in 2025, and the estate says it was Britain's tallest tree for a number of years before a Douglas fir near Inverness overtook it. In Diana's Grove at Blair Castle, another reached 62.70 metres in 2009, then the second tallest tree in the UK. Outside Rouen, the Five Brothers in the Forêt Verte have climbed 39 metres in about fifty years. Only Seattle's grows at home. When Fujitaro Kubota bought his logged land in 1927, this fir was one of the few trees left standing, and the garden he built went in around it.
